extracted.intended_audience: humor researchers, linguists, and cognitive psychologists studying verbal jokes
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical framework (General Theory of Verbal Humor, GTVH) for analyzing and representing verbal jokes via six Knowledge Resources (KRs), their hierarchy, invariants/variants, and production/processing components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Knowledge Resources (six-argument joke template)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke is represented by a six-argument template: {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA} (Script Opposition, Logical Mechanism, Situation, Target, Narrative Strategy, Language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In GTVH each variance relation between jokes is indexed by which argument KRs the two jokes share; a six-argument invariant uniquely defines a particular joke. This template replaces earlier two- or five-level templates and is the core representational rubric for classifying joke variants and invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script Opposition (SO) as a primary KR
rubrics_metrics.description: SO identifies the two (partially) overlapping scripts in a joke and the oppositeness relation between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO has been central in SSTH and higher-level invariants (e.g., {SO} or {SO, LM}) are often useful for generalizations. SO and LM are placed at the top levels in GTVH, reflecting their primacy in determining joke type and invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical Mechanism (LM) as a KR
rubrics_metrics.description: LM specifies the cognitive/logical operation (e.g., figure-ground reversal, negation, chiasmus, false priming) that connects the scripts and produces the humorous effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors caution about ambiguity in 'logical' labeling: LM covers mechanisms often discussed with logical terminology but may be better considered 'cognitive'. Figure-ground reversal is to be used in a constrained sense (a REAL vs. UNREAL role swapping for some elements), distinguishing perceptive/Gestaltic, denotative, and 'relational inversion' senses to avoid overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation (SI) as a KR
rubrics_metrics.description: SI encodes the situational context(s) in which the joke occurs (serial templates, the actual occurring Situation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SItuational (or 'situation(al)') jokes are produced out of their components: the Situation may provide some components explicitly/implicitly and the producer supplies the rest. Certain serial templates (e.g., light-bulb jokes) are captured by fixing SI or other arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target (TA) as a KR
rubrics_metrics.description: TA identifies the target(s) of the joke (e.g., social groups, stereotypes, ethnic targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TA draws on disciplines like sociology, psychology, history, and folklore; target choices contribute to invariants and affect applicability/generalization across joke variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Strategy (NS) as a KR
rubrics_metrics.description: NS assigns a macrostructure or mode of presentation (genre, narrative strategy) to the joke text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NS determines genre/style and presentation decisions (including nonredundancy/implicitness as part of presentation). It is distinct from 'language' (mechanism/style), and most crucial content-related decisions are made under NS rather than LA. NS fixes macro-choices such as riddle vs expository strategy and whether to present content implicitly or verbosely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language (LA) as a KR
rubrics_metrics.description: LA is the mechanism of language activated for expressing the joke's contents (lexical, syntactic, phonetic choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LA covers small-scale decisions (synonym choice, parapastic syntactic constructions) and phonetic properties (e.g., alliteration) that can be crucial: if a joke depends on alliteration or specific phonetics, phonetic changes may alter the punchline and take the version beyond the paraphrase range. LA is treated as the tool for implementing higher KR choices and interacts with NS.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSTH required components for joke production
rubrics_metrics.description: According to SSTH, necessary components for producing a joke are: (i) a switch from bona-fide to non-bona-fide mode; (ii) the text of the intended joke; (iii) two (partially) overlapping scripts compatible with the text; (iv) an oppositeness relation between the two scripts; (v) a trigger (obvious or implied) realizing the oppositeness relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component (i) is a precondition. Component (ii) incorporates the punchline (v). Components (iii) and (iv) pertain to SO. SSTH analyzes common cooccurrences and techniques for providing missing components in a Situation (e.g., puns as cheap triggers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy/ordering criterion for KRs
rubrics_metrics.description: The theoretical ordering (hierarchy) of KRs is based on asymmetric influences among KRs and similarity relations, not on the temporal order of joke production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A linear ordering of KRs is a convenient way to combine pairwise hierarchical relations; however partial orderings may be necessary. Empirical production order (what a speaker starts with) has no bearing on the theoretical hierarchy because production is not equivalent to analysis/generation levels; lower-level KRs are not temporally later. A modified content/tool dichotomy is proposed where some tool-oriented KRs may serve only particular content KRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paraphrase/joke sameness as a fuzzy/prototype criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke sameness (paraphrase equivalence) is not binary but fuzzy: paraphrases fall within a 'range' of equivalence and share varying degrees of closeness; some variants are closer than others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors invoke prototype and fuzzy-set theory: there is a cutoff point beyond which a version is no longer a paraphrase of the same joke. Variants/invariants in GTVH are defined by which KRs are shared; higher-level invariants (e.g., {SO, LM}) will often be more useful for generalizations than accidental lower-level matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsifiability and revision criteria for GTVH
rubrics_metrics.description: GTVH must be falsifiable: it can be falsified theoretically by discrediting a KR or adding a new KR, or empirically if experiments contradict GTVH's similarity-related conjectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An empirical falsification would be, e.g., if subjects reliably consider two-difference jokes more similar than one-difference jokes, or if pairs differing in higher KRs are judged more similar than those differing in lower KRs. Theoretical revision (replace/add KR) constitutes falsification leading to theory revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance/justification requirement for perceived humor (Aubouin's criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor perception requires not only incongruity but also acceptance/justification: two incongruous objects must be simultaneously 'accepted' for the situation to elicit humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aubouin describes 'justification' as masking that allows brief/superficial acceptance of the absurdity; acceptance may involve an 'error of judgment' or 'paralogic'. Causes include errors of judgment (similarities, poor observation, prejudice, etc.) and language-linked errors (sound similarities, ambiguities, literal interpretations, puns, alliterations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope constraint: GTVH addresses the 'what' question for verbal humor
rubrics_metrics.description: GTVH is a general, essentialist theory addressing 'what is humor?' specifically for verbal humor (represented by jokes); it does not aim to explain 'why humor exists' or 'how people use humor'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors note GTVH's affinity to incongruity-based theories but emphasize it is better defined and less tied to particular psychological baggage (e.g., arousal-resolution). They also argue the theory can be extended to handle many types of verbal humor (metalinguistic items, parodies), albeit some phenomena (e.g., alliteration) may require special attention under the LA parameter.
